## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this 

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

## Part 1: Data Processing

Write a function to GET() the URL, parse the JSON, and pull out a list of the variables with their values. (BaseR list manipulations is the easiest way to go here!)


```{r}
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(tidyverse)


obtain_url_info <- function(url){
  output <- GET(url)
  parsed <- fromJSON(rawToChar(output$content))$variables
  
  new_df <- data.frame(
    AGEP = parsed$AGEP,
    GASP = parsed$GASP,
    GRPIP = parsed$GRPIP, 
    JWAP = parsed$JWAP, 
    JWDP = parsed$JWDP, 
    JWMNP = parsed$JWMNP, 
    PWGTP = parsed$PWGTP, 
    FER = parsed$FER, 
    HHL = parsed$HHL, 
    SCH = parsed$SCH, 
    SCHL = parsed$SCHL, 
    SEX = parsed$SEX, 
#    ST = parsed$ (for 2021, 2022) / STATE (for 2023, 2024), 
    REGION = parsed$REGION, 
    DIVISION = parsed$DIVISION
  )

}
```

```{r}
result <- obtain_url_info("https://api.census.gov/data/2021/acs/acs1/pums/variables.json")
result
```
